sections.en: The mishna continues its discussion of the speech given before battle. “And the officers shall speak further to the people, and they shall say: What man is there that is fearful and fainthearted? Let him go and return unto his house” (Deuteronomy 20:8). Rabbi Akiva says: “That is fearful and fainthearted” is to be understood as it indicates, that the man is unable to stand in the battle ranks and to see a drawn sword because it will terrify him. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: “That is fearful and fainthearted”; this is one who is afraid because of the sins that he has; he, too, returns. Therefore, the Torah provided him with all these additional reasons for exemption from the army so he can ascribe his leaving to one of them. In this way, the sinner may leave the ranks without having to publicly acknowledge that he is a sinner. Rabbi Yosei says: With regard to one who has betrothed a woman forbidden to him, including a widow betrothed to a High Priest; a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza] betrothed to a common priest; a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman betrothed to an Israelite; or a daughter of an Israelite betrothed to a mamzer or a Gibeonite; this man is he whom the verse calls “fearful and fainthearted.” He fears that his sin will jeopardize his safety in the war.
sections.he: (שם כ) וְיָסְפוּ הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וְאָמְרוּ מִי הָאִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב יֵלֵךְ וְיָשֹׁב לְבֵיתוֹ. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב, כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמֹד בְּקִשְׁרֵי הַמִּלְחָמָה וְלִרְאוֹת חֶרֶב שְׁלוּפָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר, הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב זֶהוּ הַמִּתְיָרֵא מִן הָעֲבֵרוֹת שֶׁבְּיָדוֹ, לְפִיכָךְ תָּלְתָה לוֹ הַתּוֹרָה אֶת כָּל אֵלּוּ, שֶׁיַּחֲזֹר בִּגְלָלָן. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט, מַמְזֶרֶת וּנְתִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַמְזֵר וּלְנָתִין, הֲרֵי הוּא הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב:

en: זְקִיפִין, זְקוֹפִין m. plural (זָקַף) officers for restoring the line of battle, guards against desertions. Sotah VIII, 6 (44ᵃ זקי׳; Yerushalmi ed. זְקוֹפִים, Rashi זוֹקְפִין). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 98 זעקפי מלחמה (read זְקִיפֵי or זוֹקְפֵי).

כַּשִּׁיל m. (Biblical Hebrew; כָּשַׁל) a carpenter’s tool for chipping, axe. Bava Kamma X, 10 ובכ׳ של בעה"ב when working with the axe, the chips belong to the owner, contradistinguished to מעצד. Ib. 119ᵇ, see חֲצִינָא.—plural כַּשִּׁילִים, כַּשִּׁילִין. Sotah VIII, 6 כ׳ של ברזל iron axes (as a weapon in war). Sifré Devarim 337 כשלים (correct accordingly).

נְפִילָה f. (נָפַל)
1) falling. Sotah VIII, 6, and e. see נִיסָה. Bava Kamma V, 7 (54ᵇ) לנְפִילַת הבור as to the laws relating to an animal falling into a pit (Shemot XXI, 33 sq.). Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 3ᵈ top שתסמכנו מנְפִילָתֵנוּ that thou mayest support us in our downfall.—plural נְפִילוֹת. Yalkut Esther 1058 (reference. to Esther VI, 13) שתי נ׳ הללו למה why this double use of nafal?

—2) (see מַפּוֹלֶת) quantity of seed required for a field. Peah V, 1 נותן לעניים (ב) כדי נ׳ (Yerushalmi ed. נִפְלָהּ לעניים) he must give to the poor as much as the field requires for seed (see Maimonides and l.; oth. opinion: as much as is generally dropped at cutting); Bava Metzia 105ᵇ. Ib. IX, 5 אם יש בה כדי נ׳ (Yerushalmi ed. נִיפְלָהּ) if the field yields as much as is required for seed, explained Yerushalmi ib. 12ᵃ כדי הזרע הנופל בה; Yerushalmi Peah. V, 18ᵈ כדי ניפלת (correct accordingly).—[Yerushalmi Orlah I, 60ᵈ top כדי נפילתה Rabbenu Shimshon to Orlah I, 2, see טְפִילָה.]

נִיסָה f. (נוּס) flight. Sotah VIII, 6 שתחלת נ׳ נפילה, corrected ib. 44ᵇ (as in Yerushalmi ed.) שתחלת נפילה נ׳ for the beginning of falling (in slaughter) is the rout; Yerushalmi ib. VIII, end, 23ᵃ; Sifré Devarim 198 שתחלת נ׳ נפילה for the beginning of flight means falling.

עֵרֶךְ m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding)
1) order, arrangement. Nedarim 22ᵇ שעֶרְכָּהּ של ארץ ישראל הוא because it (the Book of Joshua) contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel.—plural עֲרָכִים, constr. עֶרְכֵי. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VI, 4; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Vayhi, p. 7ᵃ sq. שש ע׳ המשנה, see מִשְׁנָה.—ע׳ המלחמה order of battle, arrangements proclaimed before the battle (see מַעַרְכִים). Yerushalmi Sotah VIII, beginning 22ᵇ (reference. to Mishnah ib. VIII, 6) אבל בע׳ המ׳ מספקין וכ׳ but in connection with the proclamation of the regulations of battle (the Mishnah says only), ‘they have to supply water &c.’ Ib. אף בע׳ המ׳ כן the same is the case with ordinances of battle (they must be proclaimed in Hebrew). Bavli Sotah 43ᵇ אין חוזרין עליו מע׳ המ׳ they are not entitled to leave the army on that account. Ib. 44ᵇ; Menachot 36ᵃ; and e.

—2) valuation, assessment, value of a person or animal dedicated to the sanctuary; vow of value. Arakhin 7ᵇ ואמר עֶרְכִּי עלי if he says, I vow my own value. Ib. IV, 1 הע׳ בזמן הע׳ the valuation is regulated by the time of the vow (irrespective of the value at the time of paying the vow); ib. 4 נותן כזמן הע׳ he pays according to the value at the time of the vow. Ib. נותן ע׳ זקן he pays the value of an old man (Vayikra XXVII, 7); ע׳ ילד the value of a child (ib. 6); and from—plural עֲרָכִים, עֲרָכִין. Ib. II, 1 אין בע׳ וכ׳ (Variant נֶעֱרָכִין, see עָרַךְ) in vows of value nothing is valued at less than a Selʿa &c.; ib. 7ᵇ כל ע׳ שאתה מעריך וכ׳ all values which you assess shall be no less than &c. Ib. IV, 1 והע׳ בנערך the vows of value are regulated by the condition of the person whose value is vowed. Ib. III, 1 יש בע׳ להקל וכ׳ in the laws regulating the dedication of values there is a lenient and a rigorous side. Ib. 2ᵃ, and e. כל שישנו בדמים ישנו בע׳ … אינו בע׳ he whose person has a value, can vow the value of a person or an animal, but he whose person has no value cannot. Kerith. 13ᵇ דמין וע׳, see דָּמִים. Midrash Tanḥuma Bechukotai 6 פרשת ע׳ the section treating of vows of value. Ib. בזכות הע׳ אני מציל וכ׳ as a reward for your offerings of values, I will save you &c.; and from—ʿĂrakhin, name of a treatise of Mishnah, Tosefta and Talmud Babli, of the Order of Kodashim.—[ערכין, Gittin 44ᵃ Arukh, see עַרְכִי.]

עָקֵב (Biblical Hebrew; עקב, compare עכב , to be curved)
1) heel. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 2ᶜ top; Shabbat 62ᵇ, see גּוּדָל. Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 3 אני דורך גיתה … בעֲקֵב רגלי I shall tread Edom’s vat with the heel of my foot (see Isaiah LXIII, 1 sq.). Yevamot XII, 1 סנדל שיש לו ע׳ a sandal which has a sole with a covering for the heel. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 22 מתלא בעֲקֵיבוֹ swinging his heel (dandy-like); Yalkut Mishlei 961 מתלה בעֲקֵיבָיו (plural). Zevachim VI, 3 (63ᵇ) יורדין על הע׳ (Mishnah ed. חוזרים לע׳, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 200); Sukkah 48ᵇ חוזרין על הע׳ they turn around on their heels, i.e. go back the same way. Yalkut Jeremiah 272 דשו בע׳ trod with the heel, i.e. ignored it wilfully. Midrash Till. to Psalms IV, 7, שׁוּף II. Midrash Till. to Psalms XCII, see שׁוּף I; and from

—2) (compare עֲגָבָה) haunch with thigh, posteriors. Nedarim 20ᵃ המסתכל בעֲקֵבָהּ של אשה, explained ib. במקום הטנופת שהוא מכוון כנגד ע׳ (Arukh במקום התורפה) he who gazes at the posteriors which correspond (in shape and position) to the heel. Nazir 51ᵃ רקב הבא מן הע׳ decayed matter that seems to come from the posteriors, Rashi (Tosafot: the heel).

—3) rear-guard. Sotah VIII, 6 (44ᵃ) עקבו של עם (Yerushalmi and Bavli ed. עקיבו) the rear of the people.—plural עֲקֵבִים, עֲקֵבִין. Sanhedrin 108ᵇ הוא מביא לכם מבין עִקְבֵי רגליכם he will bring you (the flood) from under your heels. Midrash Tanḥuma Ekeb 1 מצות … ומשליכין אותן תחת עִקְבֵיהֶן minor laws which people disregard and throw under their heels. Nazir 22ᵇ הריני נזירה בעִיקְבַיִךְ I will be a Nazarite following thy heels (example); הריני בעיקביך I will follow thy example; and e.—עִקְּבוֹת foot-steps. Sotah IX, 15 (49ᵇ) (in Chald. dict.) בע׳ משיחא (borrowed from Psalms LXXXIX, 52) in the footsteps of (events paving the way to) the Messiah.—[Snh. l. common gender. ועקב שמו, see עָקוֹב].

קָפַח
1) (compare (compare גבח, כופח) to arch, bend.—Denom. קִיפֵּחַ.

—2) to slap (with the palm of the hand); to strike. Yalkut Breishit 79 קְפָחַתָּהּ, see טָפַח I. Yerushalmi Yevamot XV, 14ᵈ אין החמה קוֹפַחַת על וכ׳ the sun strikes the head of man only in the harvesting season. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to I, 6 קְפָחַתּוֹ החמה על וכ׳ the sun struck his head, and his face became bronzed. Ib. VI, 10.—Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 67 (reference. to Breishit XXVII, 46) קופחת זו לזו וזו לזו slapping this against that, and that against this’ i.e. (compare נָקַשׁ) believing all of them equally bad.—[Yerushalmi Shabbat XX, end, 17ᵈ קפוח, see next. word—Horayot 11ᵇ, see infra.]

Piël - קִיפֵּחֵ
1) same. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 23 (reference. to וזה, Breishit XI, 6) ק׳ על ראשו וכ׳ he put his hand upon Nimrod’s head, saying, this man &c.; ib. section (Parashah) 26.

—2) to bend, force, outrage, overwhelm. Pesachim 118ᵃ הקב"ה איֹנו מְקַפֵּחַ שכר וכ׳ the Lord does not outrage (by withholding) the reward of any creature, i.e. even the wicked are rewarded for what good they may do; Nazir 23ᵇ אין … מקפח אפי׳ שכר וכ׳ God does not withhold the reward even for a decorous word. Yerushalmi Demai I, 22ᵃ איפשר … והוא מְקַפְּחוֹ במים(= מק׳ שכרו) is it possible? he honored his Creator with water, and he should outrage him with water (allow his daughter to be drowned)?; Yerushalmi Shekalim V, 48ᵈ bottom of page מקפתו (correct accordingly). Kiddushin 52ᵇ לקַפְּחֵנִי בהלכות וכ׳ they come to overwhelm me with citations of traditions (of which they will prove me to be ignorant); Nazir 49ᵇ. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 9 (31) קִיפְּחָה נזירות בראשה she forced the nazarite obligations upon her head (the vow was of her own doing); and from—Part. pass. מְקוּפָּח; f. מְקוּפַּחַת forced, perverted, distorted. Yerushalmi Sotah III, 18ᵈ bottom of page נמצאת מידת הדין מק׳ justice would appear perverted; Bamidabar Rabbah l. common gender. Oholot XVI, 1 אקפח … שזו הלכה מק׳ may I bury my children (see infra), if this is not a distorted (misrepresented) hălakhah; Tosefta ib. XV, 12.

—3) to overpower, take from one by force. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin VIII, 26ᵇ bottom of page יושב … ומקפח הבריות וכ׳ he will sit at cross-roads and rob the people and kill &c.; (Bavli ib. 72ᵃ ומלסטם); Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 30 ומק׳ לעוברים ושבים. Yoma 83ᵇ קִפַּחְתָּ את הרועה thou hast forced the shepherd (to give thee his bread); אני קִפַּחְתִּי … ואתה קפחת וכ׳ I laid the shepherd under contribution, but thou didst so to the whole town (when they all came to his rescue with refreshments). Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 3 ראה כמה קי׳ לוט וכ׳ see to what extent Lot deprived Abraham of the divine communication!; and from

—4) to cover, bury, survive. Oholot l. common gender.; Yerushalmi Shabbat XVI, 15ᶜ bottom of page אֲקַפֵּחַ את בניי וכ׳ may I bury my children if &c. (an oath frequently used by R. Ṭarfon). Bava Metzia 85ᵃ אותו צדיק שהיה מקפח את בניו that righteous man (Ṭarfon) who used to swear by the life of his children. Pesachim 87ᵇ אין לך כל נביא … שלא ק׳ וכ׳ there was not a single prophet that did not survive four kings &c.; and from—Transferred a) to ruin. Shabbat 147ᵇ חמרא … קִיפְּתוּ וכ׳ the wine of P’rugitha and the baths of D. (luxurious life) ruined ten tribes of Israel. Kiddushin IV, 14 (82ᵃ); Tosefta ib. V, 15 קיפחתי את פרנסתי I have ruined my livelihood (forfeited the privilege of support without toil like dumb animals); Yerushalmi ib. IV, end, 66ᵈ (not קופחתי).—b) to cover up, retain. Keritot 5ᵃ bottom of page קלט את הריח וקִיפְּחוֹ the oil resorbed the scent and retained it; Horayot 11ᵇ קולט … וקפחו (ed. Venice וקופיחו; correct accordingly); Yalkut Shemot 387 (not וקיפחן).

—5) (denominative of קִפֵּחַ) to make high and arched shoulders, to cause or pretend to be humpbacked. Sotah VIII, 6 כל המבקש … לקַפֵּחַ את שוקיו if anybody attempted to go back (desert the army), he (the officer) was empowered to beat him until he was humpbacked; Sifré Devarim 198; Yalkut ib. 923. Tosefta Peah lV, 14 המקפח את שוקיו (a beggar) who simulates a hump; Ketubot 68ᵃ; Yerushalmi Peah VIII, 21ᵇ top המנפח (read: המְכַפֵּחַ).

comments.en: When the officials have finished addressing the troops, army commanders shall assume command of the troops.
comments.he: וְהָיָ֛ה כְּכַלֹּ֥ת הַשֹּׁטְרִ֖ים לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־הָעָ֑ם וּפָ֥קְד֛וּ שָׂרֵ֥י צְבָא֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם׃ {ס}

comments.en: The bearer of the news replied, “Israel fled before the Philistines and the troops also suffered a great slaughter. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the Ark of God has been captured.”
comments.he: וַיַּ֨עַן הַֽמְבַשֵּׂ֜ר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָ֤ס יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְגַ֛ם מַגֵּפָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה הָיְתָ֣ה בָעָ֑ם וְגַם־שְׁנֵ֨י בָנֶ֜יךָ מֵ֗תוּ חׇפְנִי֙ וּפִ֣ינְחָ֔ס וַאֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים נִלְקָֽחָה׃ {פ}

comments.en: The Philistines attacked Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and [many] fell on Mount Gilboa.
comments.he: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים נִלְחָמִ֣ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּנֻ֜סוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּפְּל֥וּ חֲלָלִ֖ים בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְבֹּֽעַ׃

sections.en: The mishna continues its discussion. The verse states: “And it shall be, when the officers conclude speaking to the people, that captains of legions shall be appointed at the head of the people” (Deuteronomy 20:9). The mishna adds: As well as at the rear of the people. The officers station guards [zekifin] in front of them, and other guards behind them, and they have iron rods [kashilin] in their hands. And with regard to anyone who attempts to turn back and flee from the war, the guard has license to beat [lekape’aḥ] his legs because the beginning of fleeing is a downfall on the battlefield, as it is stated: “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been also a great slaughter among the people” (I Samuel 4:17), and likewise it says further on: “And the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in Mount Gilboa” (I Samuel 31:1).
sections.he: (שם) וְהָיָה כְּכַלֹּת הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם וּפָקְדוּ שָׂרֵי צְבָאוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ הָעָם, וּבַעֲקֵבוֹ שֶׁל עָם. מַעֲמִידִין זְקִיפִין לִפְנֵיהֶם, וַאֲחֵרִים מֵאֲחוֹרֵיהֶם, וְכַשִּׁילִין שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל בִּידֵיהֶן, וְכָל הַמְבַקֵּשׁ לַחֲזֹר, הָרְשׁוּת בְּיָדוֹ לְקַפֵּחַ אֶת שׁוֹקָיו, שֶׁתְּחִלַּת נִיסָה נְפִילָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמואל א ד) נָס יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וְגַם מַגֵּפָה גְדוֹלָה הָיְתָה בָעָם, וּלְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר (שם לא) וַיָּנֻסוּ אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִפְּנֵי פְלִשְׁתִּים וַיִּפְּלוּ חֲלָלִים וְגוֹ':

comments.en: There are those who go out and return, who go out and do not return, and there are those who do not go out at all. All those about whom they said "They go out and return," they pay city taxes, and they provide water and food for the battle, and they repair the roads. All the rest are those who do not return. All those about whom they said "They do not go out at all": [If] he builds a house and inaugurates it but twelve months did not pass, he planted a vineyard and deconsecrated it but twelve months did not pass, [or] he betrothed a woman and took her [as a wife] but twelve months did not pass, these do not pay city taxes, and they do not provide water and food for the battle, and they do not repair the roads. Rabbi Yehuda would designate an optional war as a "war of mitzvah," but for an obligatory war, everyone goes out, even a bridegroom from his chamber and a bride from her wedding canopy.
comments.he: יש יוצאין וחוזרין יוצאין ואין חוזרין ויש שאין יוצאין כל עיקר כל אלו שאמרו יוצאין וחוזרין נותנין [פסי] העיר ומספקין מים ומזון למלחמה ומתקנים את הדרכים ושאר כולן אין חוזרין כל אלו שאמרו אין יוצאין כל עיקר הבונה בית וחנכו ולא שהה שנים עשר חדש נטע כרם וחללו ולא שהה שנים עשר חדש ארס אשה ולקחה ולא שהה שנים עשר חדש הללו אין נותנין פסי העיר ואין מספקין מים ומזון למלחמה ואין מתקנים את הדרכים ר' יהודה היה קורא למלחמת הרשות מלחמת מצוה אבל מלחמת חובה הכל יוצא אפי' חתן מחדרו וכלה מחופתה.

כל אילו שאמרו אין יוצאין כל עיקר, כגון הבונה בית וחנכו ולא שהה שנים עשר חודש, נטע כרם וחללו ולא שהה שנים עשר חודש, ארש אשה ולקחה ולא שהה שנים עשר חודש, הללו אין נותנין פסי העיר, ואין מספקין מים ומזון למלחמה, ואין מתקנין את הדרכים. ר' יהודה היה קורא למלחמת הרשות מלחמת מצוה. אבל מלחמת חובה הכל יוצא, אפי' חתן מחדרו וכלה מחופתה.

comments.en:
Gather the people,
Bid the congregation purify themselves.
Bring together the old,
Gather the babes
And the sucklings at the breast;
Let the bridegroom come out of his chamber,
The bride from her canopied couch.
comments.he: אִסְפוּ־עָ֞ם קַדְּשׁ֤וּ קָהָל֙ קִבְצ֣וּ זְקֵנִ֔ים אִסְפוּ֙ עֽוֹלָלִ֔ים וְיֹנְקֵ֖י שָׁדָ֑יִם יֵצֵ֤א חָתָן֙ מֵֽחֶדְר֔וֹ וְכַלָּ֖ה מֵחֻפָּתָֽהּ׃

en: When you take the field against your enemies, and see horses and chariots—forces larger than yours—have no fear of them, for the L<small>ORD</small> your God, who brought you from the land of Egypt, is with you.
Before you join battle, the priest shall come forward and address the troops.
He shall say to them, “Hear, O Israel! You are about to join battle with your enemy. Let not your courage falter. Do not be in fear, or in panic, or in dread of them.
For it is the L<small>ORD</small> your God who marches with you to do battle for you against your enemy, to bring you victory.”

Then the officials shall address the troops, as follows: “Is there anyone who has built a new house but has not dedicated it? Let him go back to his home, lest he die in battle and another dedicate it.
Is there anyone who has planted a vineyard but has never harvested it? Let him go back to his home, lest he die in battle and another harvest it.
Is there anyone who has paid the bride-price for a wife, but who has not yet married her? Let him go back to his home, lest he die in battle and another marry her.”
The officials shall go on addressing the troops and say, “Is there anyone afraid and disheartened? Let him go back to his home, lest the courage of his comrades flag like his.”
When the officials have finished addressing the troops, army commanders shall assume command of the troops.

sections.en: The mishna adds: In what case are all of these statements, with regard to the various exemptions from war, said? They are said with regard to elective wars. But in wars whose mandate is a mitzva, everyone goes, even a groom from his room and a bride from her wedding canopy. Rabbi Yehuda said: In what case are all of these statements, with regard to the various exemptions from war, said? They are said with regard to wars whose mandate is a mitzva. But in obligatory wars, everyone goes, even a groom from his room and a bride from her wedding canopy.
sections.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּמִלְחֶמֶת הָרְשׁוּת. אֲבָל בְּמִלְחֶמֶת מִצְוָה, הַכֹּל יוֹצְאִין, אֲפִלּוּ חָתָן מֵחֶדְרוֹ וְכַלָּה מֵחֻפָּתָהּ. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּמִלְחֶמֶת מִצְוָה. אֲבָל בְּמִלְחֶמֶת חוֹבָה, הַכֹּל יוֹצְאִין, אֲפִלּוּ חָתָן מֵחֶדְרוֹ וְכַלָּה מֵחֻפָּתָהּ:
